2025-01-15-a.headline: ND Overtakes JD Late, Wins Game 1 by 4
2025-01-15-a.recap: ND took Game 1 by 4 points, building a settlement on turn 70 to reach 10 with 3 VP cards that nobody else had seen. For a long stretch it looked like JD's game: JD took the first lead on turn 5, held the sole lead for 46% of the game, and claimed Longest Road on turn 45 to get within 3 of winning. Then LD took Longest Road away on turn 55, and ND went ahead 6 to 5 on turn 62 in the game's only lead change. JD was also the robber's favorite target, losing 8 cards to steals and 9 more to blocked hexes. ND led for just 9% of the game and still left JD and LD tied for second on 6.

2025-01-15-b.headline: LD outlasts ND in Longest Road tug of war
2025-01-15-b.recap: LD finished it on turn 76, taking Largest Army and building a settlement to reach 10, with JD and ND tied on 6. The game turned on Longest Road, which ND held from turn 39 until LD built a city and took it on turn 60, a 3 VP swing that also gave LD the lead 7 to 6. ND grabbed the road back on turn 63 and lost it again on turn 64, the last time it changed hands. ND spent 40% of the game in sole lead, more than anyone, while LD led for 21% of it. JD had 9 cards stolen and 19 blocked by the robber, and still finished level with ND.

2025-01-17-a.headline: LD Rallies From 5 Down, Outlasts JD in Seesaw
2025-01-17-a.recap: LD reached 14 VP on turn 75 with a settlement and a hidden VP card, already in the lead going into that final turn, and finished 3 clear of JD. It was a comeback from 5 VP down in a game where the lead changed hands 6 times, and JD, who spent 39% of the game in front, kept taking it back. The play of the game came on turn 51, when a settlement and an island bonus put LD ahead 10 to 9. JD answered on turn 52 with Longest Road and an 11 to 10 lead, but ND took the road away on turn 53 and LD was back in front 10 to 9. Largest Army on turn 66 put LD ahead for good at 12 to 11, and ND, who never led at any point, still finished holding Longest Road after taking it off JD twice.

2025-01-18-a.headline: JD island-hops to 14 as Longest Road bounces around
2025-01-18-a.recap: JD finished it with a settlement on turn 67, reaching 14 and ending 4 VP clear of ND after holding the lead since turn 49. That lead was the last of 4 lead changes, and it came from the play of the game: a settlement and an island bonus that put JD up 10 to 8, a 3 VP swing. From turn 33 onward, Longest Road kept bouncing between ND and LD, and it ended up with LD on turn 59. It still did not lift LD out of third on 8, in a game where LD also discarded 13 cards to 7s.

2025-01-18-b.headline: ND's 3 hidden VP cards beat JD by 1
2025-01-18-b.recap: ND won 16 to 15 on turn 92 by revealing 3 VP cards, taking the lead for the first time on the final move of the game. Until then it had been JD's game: JD spent 70% of it in sole lead and got within 3 of winning on turn 73, despite the coldest dice at the table and 13 cards discarded to 7s. ND took Longest Road on turn 44 and Largest Army on turn 80, the play of the game at a 2 VP swing, all with 14 cards blocked by the robber. JD went into the last move in sole lead and still finished 1 VP short, beaten by 3 cards nobody else could see.

2025-01-19-a.headline: LD Wins Road Tug of War, Then the Game
2025-01-19-a.recap: LD reached 15 on turn 74 with a settlement and an island bonus, winning by 4 over ND. LD took the first lead on turn 18 and nobody else ever held it alone, even though LD lost 6 cards to the robber, the most at the table, and discarded 9 cards to 7s. The real fight was over Longest Road: LD took it from a guest on turn 34 for a 2 VP swing, lost it back on turn 56 and took it again on turn 58. ND claimed Largest Army on turn 67 and looked like the bigger threat going into the final turn, but finished on 11. A guest held Longest Road twice without building a single settlement and finished on 2 VP.

2025-01-26-a.headline: JD Shrugs Off the Robber, Edges ND by 1
2025-01-26-a.recap: JD won 16 to 15 with a settlement on turn 103, the final turn of the game. The big swing came on turn 76: LD had taken Longest Road and the lead on turn 47, and JD took the road back to go up 11 to 8, a 4 VP swing. JD did all this as the robber's favorite target, losing 8 cards to steals and having 27 more blocked. ND had the best opening at 22 dots and finished 1 VP short without ever holding the lead alone.

2025-02-02-a.headline: Last-Turn City Lifts LD Past JD and ND

2025-02-12-a.headline: ND's hidden VP card undoes JD's late lead

2025-02-13-a.headline: JD Settles It on the Final Turn

2025-02-16-a.headline: JD Pries Longest Road From MB on Final Turn

2025-02-28-a.headline: AT turns weakest opening into 5-point rout

2025-03-05-a.headline: ND Reclaims Largest Army, Wins on Final Turn

JD went ahead 3 to 2 that early, took Longest Road at turn 22 and was sole leader for 76% of the game, while DH and LD never held the sole lead at all. JD lost 7 cards to theft, the most of anyone, but collected 78 cards from dice against 75 expected and never had to slow down. DH still took second despite the weakest opening at 19 dots and the coldest dice, collecting 49 cards against 57 expected.

2026-10-13-b.headline: AT turns weakest opening into 6-point blowout
2026-10-13-b.recap: AT won Through the Desert on turn 86 with Largest Army and 2 hidden VP cards, finishing 14 to 8 over MS after already leading going into that turn. AT started from the weakest opening at the table, 18 dots, and still led for 76% of the game. The only real wobble came on turns 57 and 58, when JD took Longest Road from AT and MS went ahead 7 to 6. AT answered on turn 62 with a settlement and an island bonus, a 3 VP swing that made it 9 to 7, and nobody took the lead back after that. JD held Longest Road to the end but finished third on 7 VP, with the coldest dice at the table: 57 cards against 85 expected.

2026-10-14-a.headline: ND answers late Longest Road swipe with winning city
2026-10-14-a.recap: ND won game 92 with a city on the final turn, finishing on 14 to LD's 11 after spending 74% of the game in sole lead. The one real scare came on turn 63, when LD took Longest Road, held by ND since turn 17, and with it the lead, 10 to 9. LD's spell in front lasted until ND's next turn. ND had the hottest dice at the table, 71 cards against 64 expected, and was also robbed the most, losing 7 cards to the robber. At the other end, AT turned the best opening of anyone, 21 dots, into 5 VP and last place.

2026-10-14-b.headline: LD Turns Weakest Opening Into Runaway Win
2026-10-14-b.recap: LD won game 93 from the front, finishing on 15 VP to AT's 10 after leading for 81% of the game. The lead came on turn 21, when a settlement and an island bonus swung 3 VP and put LD ahead 6 to 3. LD then took Largest Army on turn 65 to answer AT's Longest Road. LD built all this from the weakest opening at the table, 16 dots, while collecting fewer cards from dice than expected and losing 16 cards to theft, more than anyone else. On turn 105 LD closed it out the same way the lead had started, with a settlement and an island bonus.

2026-11-04-a.headline: Hot Dice Carry DH Past the Weakest Opening
2026-11-04-a.recap: DH won 13 to 11, taking Largest Army on turn 83 to close out a game they had led since passing MS on turn 26. DH started with the weakest opening at the table, 16 dots, but the dice made up for it: 97 cards against 81 expected, the hottest dice in the game. MS took Longest Road from DH on turn 69 and looked like the bigger threat going into the last turn, despite losing 11 cards to the robber, and finished with 2 VP cards in hand. LD had the best opening at 22 dots, discarded 12 cards to 7s and finished on 5.

2026-11-06-a.headline: MS Island-Hops Past ND on the Final Turn
2026-11-06-a.recap: MS won 14 to 13 over ND with a settlement and an island bonus on turn 93, the last turn of the game. MS had trailed by as many as 5 VP and led for just 1% of the game, while ND took the lead on turn 82, got within 3 of winning and looked like the likelier winner until the final move. The finish repeated turn 53, when the same kind of move, a settlement and an island bonus, gave MS the play of the game and a 3 VP swing. Islands brought MS 6 points in all. LD spent the most time in front, 33% of the game, and still finished fifth after discarding 16 cards to 7s.

2026-11-08-a.headline: LD Seals It With Longest Road on Final Turn
2026-11-08-a.recap: LD won it on turn 79 by taking Longest Road from JD, finishing on 14 with 2 VP cards nobody had seen, 4 clear of MS. JD, DH and ND each had a spell in front through the middle game until turn 54, when LD built a settlement, collected an island bonus and added a city for a 4 VP swing and a 9 to 8 lead. LD's dice ran hottest at the table, 97 cards against 88 expected, though 9 of them were stolen and 13 more went to sevens. MS opened best, took Largest Army and looked like the more dangerous player right up to the final turn. JD, with the coldest dice and 10 cards blocked by the robber, finished last and lost Longest Road on the final turn as well.

2026-11-13-a.headline: MS outlasts 7 lead changes, finishes with Largest Army
2026-11-13-a.recap: MS won it from the front, taking Largest Army from LD on turn 98 to finish on 15. Getting there took a comeback in a game where the lead changed hands 7 times: MS fell as far as 6 VP behind, and on turn 69 LD got within 3 of winning. The play of the game came on turn 90, when a settlement and an island bonus put MS back ahead 13 to 12 and swung 3 VP against the best opponent. MS did all of it while losing 11 cards to thieves, the most at the table, with another 9 blocked by the robber. AT looked like the likeliest winner on the visible board before the last turn and ended tied with ND on 13, with 3 of those points from hidden VP cards.

2026-11-14-a.headline: ND Strikes Last, Then Reveals 3 Hidden Points
2026-11-14-a.recap: ND won it on the final turn, building a settlement and taking an island bonus to go ahead 12 to 9, then revealed 3 hidden VP cards to finish on 15. Until then the game had mostly belonged to JD, who overcame the weakest opening at the table to take the lead at turn 30, added Longest Road at turn 39 and spent 47% of the game in sole lead despite being robbed of 6 cards and having 12 cards blocked by the robber. ND had the best opening and the hottest dice, +10 cards over expectation, and made the play of the game at turn 56 with a city and Largest Army for a 3 VP swing. The 15 to 9 final ranks 91st of 101 games for closeness, a blowout that stayed hidden in ND's hand until the last roll.

2026-11-14-b.headline: JD Answers DH Within One Roll, Wins New Shores
2026-11-14-b.recap: JD won by 2 points and finished it with a city on turn 79, after leading for 62% of the game. The lead changed hands 5 times, and the deciding exchange came late: DH went ahead 9 to 8 on turn 58, and JD took it back on the very next roll with a settlement and an island bonus, a 3 VP swing that made it 11 to 9. JD then added Largest Army on turn 67 to go with Longest Road. DH's late lead came despite the coldest dice at the table and 8 cards discarded to 7s. ND finished second on 12 without holding the lead alone for a single roll, and with 8 cards blocked by the robber.

2026-11-14-c.headline: ND takes game 100 with a final-turn settlement
2026-11-14-c.recap: ND won game 100 with a settlement on the final turn, the same turn ND took Longest Road back from JD to finish on 14. The key turn was 48, when a settlement and an island bonus made a 3 VP swing and put ND ahead 11 to 10, after DH had gone up 9 to 8 on turn 43. JD had the hottest dice at the table at +9 cards but never led outright, with 8 cards blocked by the robber and 5 more stolen. JD took Largest Army on turn 52 and still looked like the bigger threat going into the last turn, then finished third on 10.

2026-11-14-d.headline: Hidden VP card hands ND the closest game yet
2026-11-14-d.recap: ND won by revealing a hidden VP card on turn 76, finishing on 14 to JD's 13. It was the closest of the group's 101 games, with 6 lead changes and Longest Road passing back and forth between MS, ND and JD. ND spent just 5% of the game in sole lead, and going into the last turn the visible points made DH look like the most dangerous player, after DH turned the weakest opening into the hottest dice. JD finished 1 VP short after having 14 cards blocked by the robber and discarding 10 to 7s.

2026-11-15-a.headline: DH rallies from 6 down despite the coldest dice
2026-11-15-a.recap: DH won it on the final turn with a settlement, reaching 14 and finishing 2 clear of JD and ND, who tied for second on 12. It was a comeback from as many as 6 VP down, and DH did it with the coldest dice at the table, collecting 81 cards from rolls against 89 expected. The groundwork came on turn 37, when a settlement and an island bonus made a 3 VP swing, and DH finally took the lead 11 to 10 on turn 69. ND spent 42% of the game alone in front and came away with a share of second place. MS had the best opening at 19 dots and finished 4th.

2026-11-19-a.headline: JD Strikes Late, Takes Game 103 by 2
2026-11-19-a.recap: JD won with 14 VP to LD's 12, taking the lead on turn 72 and closing it out on turn 82 with a city. Until then the lead changed hands 6 times, with AT holding it longest and winning Longest Road back from ND along the way. LD had just gone ahead 10 to 9 on turn 70 when JD answered with a settlement, an island bonus and a city in one turn, a 4 VP swing that made it 11 to 10. Having the best opening at the table did not make it an easy ride: JD was robbed of 6 cards, more than anyone, and discarded 13 to sevens. JD spent only 13% of the game in the lead, which turned out to be the right 13%.

2026-11-24-a.headline: ND Shrugs Off MS Surge, Wins by 4
2026-11-24-a.recap: ND reached 14 with a city on turn 84, finishing 4 clear of MS after leading for 55% of the game. It was not a straight line: on turn 58 MS took Longest Road from ND and the lead with it, 9 to 5. ND answered on turn 76 with a city, a settlement and an island bonus in a single turn, a 4 VP swing that put ND back in front 11 to 9. ND won despite losing the most cards to the robber at 7, while MS and LD each discarded 12 cards to 7s. JD had the roughest night, starting from the weakest opening at 15 dots and getting 14 fewer cards from the dice than expected.

2026-11-24-b.headline: ND Retakes Longest Road to Close Out Desert Race
2026-11-24-b.recap: ND won it on the final turn, taking Longest Road back from JD on turn 68 to finish on 14, with LD stuck on 11. The finish came fast: LD took the lead 11 to 9 on turn 63, and JD took Longest Road from ND a turn later. ND answered on turn 65 with a city, a settlement and an island bonus, a 4 VP swing, then took the road back to close it out. LD had the hottest dice at the table at +14 cards, while ND lost the most to the robber at 7 cards and still led for 59% of the game. JD held Longest Road from turn 64 to turn 68, which mostly gave ND something to take back.
